title: School Children Who Also Hold Chapter 35: Disability Compensation Dependent Additions
content:
A child who holds Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (Chapter 35) and is paid it for an enrollment cannot also be recognized as a school child on the veteran's Disability Compensation award for the same months, because a school child may not be paid as a dependent for the same months the child is paid Chapter 35 education benefits. The child elects which benefit to take, and the school-child addition starts or stops with the first month the Chapter 35 enrollment does not cover.

A child under the child age limit can be paid as a minor child on the award regardless of Chapter 35 status.

**Cases (hypothetical)**

| Child | Chapter 35 paid for the months | Recognition on the award for those months |
|---|---|---|
| Age 19, enrolled, paid Chapter 35 for the fall term | Yes | Not as a school child for the fall-term months |
| Same child, spring term not covered by a Chapter 35 enrollment | No | The school-child addition can start with the first month the Chapter 35 enrollment does not cover |
| Age 17, Chapter 35 paid | Yes | Can be paid as a minor child |
